subject: Re: MAP draft — Legal redlines & MSA/DPA/SLA responsibilities
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft — Legal redlines & MSA/DPA/SLA responsibilities

Hi John / Acme team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment on scope and the pilot sizing. Attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we discussed (Redwood_MAP_Draft_20250620.xlsx). High level recap and next steps focused on the LEGAL milestone so we can keep to the target close: 2025-07-10.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
- Discovery & Sizing: complete (owner: Acme / sales)
- Security review (questions/attestation): owner: Acme security / Redwood security; dependency: SOC2 evidence (Redwood to share)
- Legal redlines (MSA/DPA/SLA): owner: split — Acme legal to propose redlines, Redwood legal to own the final execution & counters; turnaround times below.
- Procurement (PO / terms): owner: Acme procurement
- Pilot start & success criteria: owner: Acme product + Redwood solutions

For the legal milestone specifically, suggested responsibilities and turnaround targets:
- Acme legal to send initial redline set (tracked changes) — target: within 3 business days from today if possible.
- Redwood legal (Lauren) to do an initial pass and provide proposed counters — target: 3 business days after receiving Acme redlines.
- Technical/SLA items requiring engineering input: Redwood engineering owner (Aditya) to respond to SLA-specific metrics and feasibility within 3 business days of Lauren's request.
- Final negotiation cycles: aim for no more than 2 review cycles between legal teams to hit target close (2025-07-10).

Open dependencies:
- Acme to confirm any required data residency or audit provisions now so we can surface to infra/security.
- Procurement PO cadence (if PO needed) — please confirm expected timeline.

Can you confirm that assignment (Acme legal owns initial edits; Redwood legal owns counters) and the turnaround targets above? If OK, we’ll update the MAP and put the Legal redlines milestone with owners and dates.

Thanks — I’ll loop Lauren and Aditya on the thread so they can confirm turnaround.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_Draft_20250620.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-06-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft — Legal redlines & MSA/DPA/SLA responsibilities

Marissa — thanks for the summary.

Redwood legal will pick up ownership of producing the initial counter once we receive Acme's tracked redlines. To be explicit on SLAs for legal reviews: our team can commit to an initial pass within 48-72 business hours (2-3 business days) of receiving the redline document. For items that require engineering input (SLA metrics, uptime targets, data residency), we'll route to Aditya and expect an additional 2-3 business days for technical validation.

If Acme prefers, we can accept edits in a single Word doc and use Track Changes; we will return a single consolidated counter (not piecemeal comments) to keep cycles tight.

I'll be the Redwood legal point — cc'd on this thread.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2025-06-23T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Acme redlines (initial) — MSA/DPA/SLA

Marissa / Redwood,

Thanks for sending the MAP. Attached are Acme's initial redlines (Acme_Redlines_v1.docx). High level themes our legal team redlined:
- Data residency & cross-border transfer obligations (we've requested explicit EU residency for EU customer data)
- Indemnification caps and carve-outs for third-party claims
- Audit and compliance rights (SOC2 report frequency and onsite audit language)
- DPA specifics: subprocessor list, deletion timing, breach notification SLA (24 hrs)
- SLA: uptime definition and SLA credits calculation; we asked to see Redwood's monitoring approach and proposed MTTR windows

We’ve tracked changes in the attached doc. Can you confirm who will own making edits in the working doc (Acme edits vs. Redwood counters) and the expected turnaround for Redwood to provide counters? Ideally we'd like to close legal terms within 5 business days, but we understand engineering input may extend that.

Regards,
John Doe
Sr. Contracts Manager | Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com
Attachment: Acme_Redlines_v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-23T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme redlines (initial) — MSA/DPA/SLA

John — really appreciate the fast turnaround from your legal team and for sending the tracked changes.

Proposed next steps to keep the MAP and timeline tight:
1) Ownership: Acme sends tracked redlines (done). Redwood legal (Lauren) will perform an initial consolidated counter in Track Changes in the same doc and return within 3 business days. We will mark items that are "technical/SLA" and route those to Aditya for engineering verification.
2) Engineering/SLA questions: Aditya will confirm feasibility on SLA metrics (MTTR, monitoring data access, uptime calc) within 3 business days of receiving Lauren's flagged items.
3) Review cycles: propose max 2 legal cycles to aim for signature by 2025-07-08. If more than two cycles required, we'll escalate to exec sponsor alignment.
4) Communication & doc control: we'll maintain a single working document in track changes. Please confirm you prefer we return the same filename with a version suffix (e.g., Acme_Redlines_v1_Redwood_v1.docx).

I’ve updated the MAP (attached: Redwood_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx) to reflect owners and target dates per above. If that all looks good I’ll lock the Legal milestone dates in HubSpot and propose a short working session to walk legal teams through any ambiguous clauses.

Proposed working session: Thu 2025-06-26 10:00 AM PT — 30 minutes. Does that work for you / your legal?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-06-24T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme redlines (initial) — MSA/DPA/SLA

Marissa / Lauren / John — quick technical confirmation from infra side:

- Data residency: we can support EU-only residency for EU customer data; we'll need an additional 5 business days to prepare the SOC2 sub-report for EU controls if Acme requires a separate report (dependency).
- SLA metrics: MTTR of 4 hours for P1 incidents is feasible if we agree on the monitoring hooks (we'll expose basic summary metrics; detailed telemetry access will require an NDA/ops access checklist).
- Encryption & key management: support KMS/HSM — confirm whether Acme wants customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed keys; that will affect timing.

I can commit to responding to Lauren's flagged SLA items within 3 business days of her initial pass. Happy to join the 6/26 working session and walk through the technical ask list.

—Aditya
